terra.problem: The text does not say there was no meeting, paperwork, or time spent considering the plan.
The passage does not say Esther had nobody else.
“Her parents aren't living anywhere” is an oddly flippant way to speak about their deaths.
“Right away” and “on day one” add timing the passage does not give.
It says Hegai doesn't send Esther anywhere, but the same verse says he transfers her to the best place in the harem.
The verse does not say Hegai moved Esther as a reward, and the best place could also have been the smallest.
“She tells nobody” goes beyond the statement that Esther did not reveal her people or lineage.
The explanation repeats that no law is mentioned without adding anything to the correction. It sounds flat.
“Wrong building” uses “wrong” about the baker's answer.
“No questions” adds a detail the passage does not give.
The passage allows a woman to take whatever she requests; it does not say every woman requests something or rules out her going empty-handed.
Being summoned by name does not necessarily mean the king speaks her name himself.
Papa talks about his own visit to a hardware store. Places outside his bakery come up as things people do, not as places he visits.
“A big crowd of fans” adds a crowd size and characterization the text does not give.
The sentences after the quotation merely repeat that everyone is more than a few. The explanation is flat.
After the quotation, the explanation only repeats that the crown goes on Esther's head. It is flat.
“Nobody ever groaned at that announcement” states an unreported reaction as fact.
A census does not necessarily require people to line up, and that detail is not in this passage.
The passage says Esther informed the king on Mordecai's behalf; it does not say she used her position as queen to do so.
“Records can matter later” hints at the record's role later in the story instead of leaving what happens next open.
The passage does not mention an announcement or messengers, but it does not say none were sent.
The passage does not say nothing was carved on the gate; it simply does not mention carving the account there.
